## Level 2: Forward-compliant

- [ ] **CORE-AI-05** (MUST) Age-appropriate AI output, tested before release. Input and output filters adapted to the target age, red-team tests in the product's languages before release, and post-release monitoring of incidents.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-AI-06** (MUST) No AI persona that simulates a relationship. AI characters are friendly but never claim feelings, friendship, missing the child, or exclusivity, and do not create emotional dependency (see CORE-AI-08 for conversation memory).  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-AI-08** (MUST) Conversation memory is off by default. AI systems do not keep or reuse information from a child's previous conversations by default, except where necessary to protect the child's safety. Any memory is visible to the teacher or guardian and can be deleted.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-AI-09** (MUST) AI is re-tested regularly and monitored after release. AI features are evaluated for risks to children before release and at regular intervals afterwards (and on every model or prompt change). After release, incidents involving children are detected, logged, assessed and acted on, with a named owner.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-AI-10** (MUST) An AI assistant inside a game or app is opt-in and easy to leave. When an AI chatbot or companion is a feature of a game, app or platform, it is not switched on automatically, not displayed prominently (e.g. not pinned at the top of contacts or the home screen), children are not encouraged to use it, and they can turn it off easily at any time.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-AI-11** (MUST) AI never nudges children to spend or towards ads. AI tutors, characters and assistants never suggest purchases, upgrades, premium content or advertised products, and are not optimised for spending or engagement time.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-03** (MUST) Moderation by people and by tools. Communication is moderated by named people (a teacher in school use, trained moderators otherwise) who can hide, remove, mute and suspend, supported by automated filters for text and images in the product's languages, with rate limits against spam. The level of moderation matches the age band.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-04** (MUST) Direct messages only with approved contacts; groups only with agreement. Nobody can start a private conversation with a child unless the child (or, under 13, the guardian or teacher) has approved that contact. Children are added to groups only with their agreement. Nobody can pressure a child into approving contact.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-05** (MUST) No links, handles or contact details in children's messages. Messages to and from children block or warn on external links, social media handles, phone numbers, emails and addresses, so the product cannot be used to move children to other services.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-06** (MUST) Voice, video and live streaming off by default. Voice chat, video chat and live streaming are off by default, enabled only by a guardian or teacher for under-13s, limited to approved contacts, and children cannot host live streams by default.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-07** (MUST) Children's shared media is protected. Images and files sent in messages are checked automatically, visible to the responsible teacher or moderator, and cannot be downloaded or forwarded by other users. Contact and account information of children is never visible to people they have not accepted.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CHT-08** (MUST) Safeguarding procedure for communication risks. There is a written safeguarding procedure with a named lead: how moderators recognise and escalate grooming, sexual exploitation, extortion, threats, self-harm signals and radicalisation; how evidence is preserved; when guardians, schools, hotlines and authorities are contacted; and how moderators are trained and supported.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-COM-02** (SHOULD) Third-party analytics and session recording reviewed. Product analytics and session-replay tools are either self-hosted in the EEA or bound by a processor agreement that forbids reuse of data. Session recording is not used on child-facing screens.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-COM-05** (MUST) Purchases are labelled as purchases, in real time. Before any purchase or spending of purchasable currency, the child is told in clear, age-appropriate words (and icons or audio for non-readers) that this is a purchase that costs real money, at the moment it happens, with the price in the national currency.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-COM-06** (MUST) No design for impulsive or unwanted spending. No one-tap or in-content purchases for children. There is a clear separation and friction between learning or play content and buying anything related to it (for example a separate adult area and a confirmation step). No spending prompts at moments of frustration, failure or excitement.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DAT-09** (MUST) Geolocation off and not collected unless essential. Precise geolocation is not collected. If a feature truly needs it, it is off by default and turned off again at the end of the session.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DAT-10** (MUST) Microphone and camera off by default. Access to microphone and camera is off by default, requested only at the moment of use for a clear learning purpose, and the recording is not kept longer than needed.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-01** (SHOULD) Motion and sound can be turned down or off. The product honours the device's reduced-motion setting and offers in-app controls to reduce animation and sound, including motion triggered by the learner's own actions.  
      Evidence:

The manifest records whether the product is in scope of the EU KIDS Act (online game, AI companion, general conversational chatbot, social or video-sharing service) or exempt as a service designed primarily for education and operated by or on behalf of an educational establishment (Art. 2(4)(c)).  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-01** (MUST) Most protective settings by default. Profiles private, sharing off, contact off, notifications off, recommendations of other users off by default. Defaults are only relaxed after age assurance shows the user is an adult.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-02** (MUST) Notifications only about the child's own activity, off by default, quiet hours. Push notifications are off by default, never designed to prompt the child to start or resume use, only relate to the child's own activity or teacher assignments, and respect school time and core sleep hours.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-03** (MUST) Natural stopping points, no autoplay or endless feeds. No autoplay of the next content and no infinite scroll. Sessions have natural endings and regular interruption moments that let the child decide whether to continue.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-06** (MUST) Child-friendly reporting and support. Wherever children interact with others or with generated content, a report option is one step away, understandable by the target age, processed with priority, and followed by information on help resources.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-07** (MUST) Tools for guardians and teachers that respect the child. Guardians (or teachers in school use) can manage settings, time and contacts. The child is told when such tools are active. Controls cannot be bypassed by the child.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-08** (MUST) Proportionate, privacy-preserving age assurance. Where age matters, age assurance is proportionate, uses zero-knowledge solutions such as the EU age verification app, does not store identity documents and only keeps an age signal. Self-declaration alone is not relied on for high-risk features.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-09** (SHOULD) Children can control and give feedback on what they see. Children can adjust settings that affect how they interact and what they are shown, give feedback with lasting effect, and easily return to default settings.  
      Evidence:

## Level 3: Best practice

- [ ] **CORE-ACC-03** (SHOULD) Inclusive design for children with special educational needs. Adjustable speed and time limits, audio alternatives for text, captions, dyslexia-friendly typography options, and support for switch or keyboard-only play.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CNT-01** (SHOULD) Asset provenance and licences recorded. Every image, sound, font and AI-generated asset has a recorded source, licence, author and, for AI assets, the model used.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-CNT-02** (SHOULD) Age rating self-assessment. The product has a documented age-appropriateness assessment covering violence, fear, language, in-app purchases, contact risks and addictive features (PEGI-style descriptors).  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-COM-08** (SHOULD) No commercial content inside learning activities for children. Learning activities for children contain no product placement, branded rewards, sponsored characters or influencer endorsements, even when labelled. Funding and partner credits, if any, appear only in adult-facing areas.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-02** (SHOULD) Motion shows the content, not decoration. Animation is used to show what is learned (a process, a change over time, a procedure). Decorative, celebratory or purely entertaining motion and interesting-but-irrelevant extras ("seductive details") are kept to a minimum.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-03** (SHOULD) Calm screens, especially under 8. Few elements compete on screen at once (as a guide, no more than four interactive or animated elements on the main screen for under-8s), and help is available as audio or pictures, not text only.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-04** (SHOULD) Fantasy does not blur facts for young children. When teaching facts about the real world to young children, use realistic images and plain language. Talking animals, impossible events and fantasy framing are kept for stories and play, not for factual content.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-05** (SHOULD) Visual style matches the concept, especially in maths. Abstract concepts use simple, schematic visuals. Graphs and diagrams carry no decorative pictures. Concrete images are used to start, then faded towards abstract representations. Pleasant colours and friendly faces are welcome where they do not compete with the content.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-06** (SHOULD) Celebrations are short and proportional. Reward animations and sounds are brief, proportional to the achievement and skippable. Win sounds are not used to make small or no progress feel like a big win.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-DES-07** (SHOULD) No colour-psychology claims. Design decisions and product claims do not rely on popular colour-psychology effects (e.g. "red lowers performance") that are not supported by robust evidence.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-GOV-03** (SHOULD) Child rights impact assessment. A child rights impact assessment (or a risk review in the sense of the DSA Art. 28 guidelines) is documented, considers the best interests of the child, and involves children, guardians and educators in testing.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SAF-04** (SHOULD) Time-awareness tools. The product offers break reminders and lets guardians or teachers set a daily time limit, protecting school time (outside class use) and core sleep hours.  
      Evidence: 
- [ ] **CORE-SEC-06** (SHOULD) Strong authentication for adults, simple safe login for children. Teacher and admin accounts use MFA. Children use age-appropriate login (class code, picture password, teacher reset) without email or phone collection.  
      Evidence:
